articles.title: Get to Know the Broker: Lauren Muss of Douglas Elliman
articles.narrative: This article profiles Lauren Muss, a prominent residential real estate broker at Douglas Elliman, highlighting her career trajectory and approach to the business. Muss, a trained gemologist, transitioned into real estate in 1994 and has since achieved over $7 billion in sales in Manhattan's high-end residential market. She emphasizes her team-based approach, where each member operates with full ownership, fostering a collaborative environment rather than a hierarchical one.

articles.title: The Power of the Public-Private Partnership for Affordable Housing
articles.narrative: This article argues that public-private partnerships are the most effective solution to the affordable housing crisis, which is exacerbated by a national shortage of 4.7 million homes and the loss of 7 million affordable rental homes since 2014. The author contends that traditional public housing authorities face structural constraints and limited budgets, while the private sector, driven by market dynamics, often leads to displacement when affordability agreements expire. The piece advocates for a collaborative approach, leveraging public policy goals with private sector expertise and capital to both build new affordable housing and, critically, preserve existing affordable units through proven financing tools like Low-Income Housing Tax Credits (LIHTCs) and tax-exempt bonds. The author emphasizes that preserving existing affordable housing is an overlooked but essential lever to address the crisis, especially given the challenges and costs associated with new construction.

articles.title: Virginia, Maryland Tighten Data Center Rules as Scrutiny Intensifies
articles.narrative: Officials in Virginia and Maryland are implementing stricter regulations on data center development across the Mid-Atlantic region. Maryland's Governor issued an executive order establishing a review process for data centers over 25 megawatts, creating a task force to evaluate projects based on their impact on ratepayers and the grid, and seeking to repeal a sales and use tax exemption. In Virginia, Prince William County has significantly reduced its Data Center Opportunity Zone Overlay District and now requires special-use permits for new proposals outside this area, while the Governor announced a broad "Data Center Accountability Framework" and is proposing legislation to eliminate by-right approval for large data centers and end state subsidies. These actions signal a shift towards increased transparency, environmental oversight, and local control over data center growth.

articles.title: Hudson Bay Capital Refis Microsoft-Anchored SoHo Building With $85M Loan
articles.narrative: InterVest Capital Partners has secured an $85 million refinancing loan from Hudson Bay Capital for its mixed-use office and retail property at 300 Lafayette Street in Manhattan's SoHo neighborhood. The seven-story building, completed in 2019, is largely anchored by a major technology company occupying the entire office component. The strong tenancy and quality of the boutique property attracted competitive lender interest, reflecting its value in the Lower Manhattan market.

data_points.address: 300 Lafayette Street, New York City, NY
data_points.project_notes: A major technology company signed a long-term lease for the office portion in March 2019, just before construction completion.

articles.title: Nomic AI Inks 5K-SF Deal at 99 University Place Near Union Square
articles.narrative: Four tenants have signed new office leases totaling 15,593 square feet at 99 University Place, a 10-story office building near Union Square in Manhattan. Design software firm Nomic AI, therapy space provider Therapeutic Alliance Suites, and construction systems developer T Moriarty & Son each secured full-floor leases of 4,890 square feet. The building's appeal stems from its prime Greenwich Village location, authentic character, high ceilings, natural light, and manageable full-floor layouts, which are increasingly sought after in a market with limited supply.

data_points.address: 99 University Place, New York City, NY
data_points.notable_features: Located near Union Square in Greenwich Village, featuring high ceilings and natural light.

articles.title: CBRE Arranges Sale of 384-Unit Apartment Community in Somerset, New Jersey
articles.narrative: CBRE has facilitated the off-market sale of The Grove at Somerset, a 384-unit apartment community in Franklin, New Jersey. The property, developed in 2013, was acquired by Los Angeles-based owner-operator TruAmerica from Harbor Group International. The community offers a mix of studio, one-, two-, and three-bedroom units, with 58 designated for affordable housing.

data_points.notable_features: Amenities include a pool with a sundeck, resident clubhouse with a lounge area, business center, fitness center, playground and a dog park. 58 units are designated as affordable housing.

articles.title: Largo Capital Places $24M Permanent Loan for Buffalo Industrial Property
articles.narrative: Largo Capital has secured a $24 million permanent loan for a 300,000-square-foot industrial property in Buffalo, NY. The nonrecourse financing was arranged through an undisclosed CMBS lender for an undisclosed borrower. The property, located in an established industrial park south of downtown, was fully leased to a single tenant at the time of closing.

data_points.notable_features: Located within an established industrial park just south of the downtown area.

articles.title: Marcus & Millichap Brokers $4M Sale of Apartment Building in Kearny, New Jersey
articles.narrative: Marcus & Millichap has brokered the $4 million sale of Helena Arms, a 17-unit apartment building in Kearny, New Jersey. The off-market transaction involved a private investor as the seller and an undisclosed buyer. Acquisition financing for the deal was also arranged by Marcus & Millichap Capital Corp.

data_points.notable_features: The three-story building consists of two studios, six one-bedroom units, and nine two-bedroom apartments.

articles.title: IPA Arranges Joint Venture Equity for Cliff at Green Valley Ranch Adaptive Reuse Project in Henderson, Nevada
articles.narrative: IPA Capital Markets has arranged joint venture equity for VAC Development's adaptive reuse project, The Cliff at Green Valley Ranch, in Henderson, Nevada. This development will transform two former office buildings into a 100,000-square-foot open-air retail, dining, and lifestyle campus, marking the first major project of its kind in Henderson since 2004. The project emphasizes experiential retail, chef-driven dining, wellness, and community gathering spaces, with tenant deliveries expected to begin in the second quarter of 2027.

data_points.property_name: The Cliff at Green Valley Ranch
data_points.notable_features: Adaptive reuse of two obsolete office buildings into a Class A, pedestrian-friendly campus with 38 units, a 26,000-square-foot covered outdoor dining lounge, landscaped courtyards, and public art.

articles.title: First Washington Realty acquires grocery-anchored shopping centers in Minnesota, Missouri
articles.narrative: First Washington Realty has expanded its portfolio with the acquisition of two grocery-anchored shopping centers, The Village of Blaine in Minnesota and Liberty Corners in Missouri, for a combined price exceeding $65 million. These acquisitions align with the buyer's strategy of investing in well-located neighborhood shopping centers that serve as essential community hubs for daily needs. The properties are expected to benefit from strong local demographics and continued investment in their respective areas.

data_points.project_notes: The combined value of the two properties is in excess of $65 million.

Marcus & Millichap brokers sale of 248-unit multifamily property in Bryan
articles.narrative: Marcus & Millichap has brokered the sale of Retreat at 2818, a 248-unit multifamily property in Bryan, Texas. A California-based real estate investment firm acquired the asset from a Texas-based private client. The buyer plans to implement a value-add strategy, investing approximately $3 million in renovations during the first year of ownership.

articles.title: Positive vibes on the menu at St. Louis Commercial Real Estate Summit
articles.narrative: The ninth annual St. Louis Commercial Real Estate Summit highlighted a cautiously optimistic outlook for the region's CRE market, despite broader economic uncertainties. Speakers noted the continued resilience of the industrial, retail, and multifamily sectors, with Class A office properties also showing positive performance. The event emphasized networking and a forward-looking perspective on the St. Louis market's future.

articles.title: Sephora Relocates Meatpacking District Store with Long-Term Lease
articles.narrative: Sephora has signed a long-term lease for 4,200 square feet of ground-floor retail space at 401 W. 14th St. in Manhattan's Meatpacking District, relocating its existing store in the neighborhood. The new location, expected to open in Q1 2027, is strategically positioned on a highly visible and trafficked retail corner, adjacent to a major tech flagship store, underscoring the importance of prime visibility for establishing a strong retail presence in this iconic shopping destination.

data_points.address: 401 W. 14th St., New York City, NY
data_points.notable_features: Located adjacent to Apple's Meatpacking District flagship store, at a prominent retail corner.

articles.title: Avatar Furnishes Bridge Loan on Fully Leased Santa Ana Warehouse
articles.narrative: Avatar Financial Group LLC provided a $4.75 million bridge loan for a fully leased warehouse and distribution building in Santa Ana, CA. The two-year, first-lien loan was originated at approximately 60% loan-to-value, replacing the property's existing first mortgage and a junior loan. The sponsor plans to secure long-term financing after approximately six months of rental income, a strategy supported by the tenant's significant investment in its build-out and the property's strong location.

data_points.address: 4001 W. Carriage Dr., Santa Ana, CA
data_points.notable_features: Located less than two miles from Interstate 405 and State Route 55.
data_points.project_notes: The financing replaced an existing first mortgage and a junior loan that had matured. The tenant invested substantially in its own build-out, and rent commenced prior to the loan closing.

articles.title: George Comfort & Sons Refinances 200 Madison for $386M
articles.narrative: George Comfort & Sons, in partnership with Loeb Partners Realty and Jamestown, has secured a $386 million refinancing for 200 Madison Avenue, a 750,000-square-foot office tower in New York City's Grand Central district. The five-year floating-rate loan, provided by New York Life, will be used to retire existing debt and support ongoing leasing efforts. This refinancing reflects the lending community's confidence in well-located, amenity-rich office properties with strong sponsorship, particularly following a significant lease extension and expansion by a major tenant.

data_points.address: 200 Madison Avenue, New York City, NY
data_points.notable_features: Located in the Grand Central district, offering top-tier amenities and an unrivaled location.
data_points.project_notes: The loan has a three-year initial term with two 12-month extension options. Proceeds will be used to pay off existing debt and fund ongoing leasing. A major tenant recently extended its headquarters lease for 15 years and expanded its footprint to 254,118 square feet.

articles.title: Zurich Affiliate Acquires San Francisco Offices with Leasing Upside
articles.narrative: An affiliate of Zurich Alternative Asset Management has acquired 410 Townsend, a 78,455-square-foot historic office building in downtown San Francisco, for $47.4 million. The seller was a joint venture between New York Life Real Estate Investors and Bridgeton Holdings. The property, built in 1912, offers significant leasing upside with its current 65% occupancy, reflecting a strengthening market for well-located, quality assets in San Francisco.

data_points.notable_features: Historic building with exposed brick and heavy timber construction, modern amenities, and flexible office layouts.

articles.title: JLL Arranges JV Equity, Acquisition Debt on Jersey City Multifamily
articles.narrative: JLL Capital Markets has arranged joint venture equity and acquisition financing for Jasmin Terrace II, a newly constructed 56-unit luxury apartment building in Jersey City. The transaction involved Tower Management Service LP, making its debut in the Jersey City market, securing a joint venture equity investment from Lakerock, forming a new partnership. JLL then secured a $16.5 million, five-year, fixed-rate acquisition loan through RWC Lending for the partnership.

data_points.notable_features: Luxury apartment building with walkable access to Jersey City's light rail network, proximity to Liberty State Park, and a rapidly maturing retail and dining scene.
data_points.project_notes: Tower Management Service LP is making its debut in the Jersey City market with this acquisition.

articles.title: Brookings Study Shows AI’s $10T Build-Out Cost Will Likely End In Market Correction
articles.narrative: New research from Brookings suggests that the development of AI infrastructure will be significantly more capital-intensive than the construction of the U.S. railway network in the 19th century. The study projects a staggering $10 trillion build-out cost for AI, a figure that raises concerns about a potential market correction. This substantial investment highlights the unprecedented scale of resources required to support the burgeoning AI industry.

articles.title: Hundreds Of Townhomes Proposed Across 2 South Philly Projects: The Philadelphia Deal Sheet
articles.narrative: Trove Capital and Hightop Development have proposed two new townhome projects in South Philadelphia, totaling 262 units. This development aims to address the demand for new residential options in the area. Additionally, two shopping centers were sold in Montgomeryville and outside Scranton, indicating continued activity in the retail investment market.

data_points.project_notes: Two separate projects proposed by the same developers.

articles.title: Austin Multifamily Nears 'Inflection Point' With Early Signs Of Rent Growth
articles.narrative: The Austin multifamily market is approaching an "inflection point" as early indicators suggest a transition from an oversupplied market to one experiencing rent growth. This shift signals a potential recovery and stabilization in rental rates after a period of significant new construction.

articles.title: Retail Is In Growth Mode Again, But Construction Isn't Keeping Up
articles.narrative: The U.S. retail sector is experiencing a significant boom in new store openings, indicating a strong period of growth. However, this expansion is being hampered by a lag in new construction, primarily driven by elevated development costs. This imbalance between demand for new retail spaces and the supply of new construction poses a challenge for retailers looking to expand their physical footprints.

articles.title: Texas, California Add New Restrictions On Data Center Development
articles.narrative: Texas and California have implemented new restrictions on data center development, responding to increasing public concern regarding the environmental and resource impact of the artificial intelligence industry. These measures reflect a broader trend of states addressing the significant energy and water demands associated with large-scale data processing facilities.
